title: When the Lights Learn Our Names

source_honesty.note: The text fixes an artistic narrative test. Its Hebrew-shaped verbs, legacy regional-looking forms, obviation markers, and grammatical commentary are not source evidence or accepted contact grammar.

protected_functions.description: Keep the comic contrast between an ordinary modern blackout and a strongly waw-driven literary narrative cadence.
Introduce Mara, Jules, and Tina as three distinct participants and preserve a coherent arc for all three.
Preserve the mounting foreground-event pulse, peak congestion, abrupt reveal, short release, and calmer coda.
Make every human action recoverable across center shifts and at least two simultaneously salient noncentral third persons.
Carry the title through failed room light, phone light, match light, lantern light, restored light, and remembered future flickers.
Retain the causal escalation of alarm, impact, ringing spoons, lid, pot, spill, slides, scattered objects, and involuntary dance.
Preserve the restored-light freeze-frame: one person on the floor, one caught with a coat, one among tools, and the pot hissing.
Resolve the chaos through affectionate shared looking and laughter rather than blame.
Mark the transition from one completed incident to a recurring response or remembered custom through the wayyiqtol-derived and weqatal-derived systems.
Make Biblical-Hebrew-derived event framing and source-specific Algonquian participant tracking function together rather than coexist as decoration.

identity_invariants: The title remains When the Lights Learn Our Names in English unless the owner makes a separate songwriting decision.
The story retains a named trio, blackout, escalating improvised lights and slapstick, restored-light tableau, shared laughter, and a recurring coda.
The main incident and final coda remain grammatically distinct so the one-time fiasco becomes remembered custom.
Names-once and minimal renaming remain valuable compression targets, but never excuse unrecoverable participants.
The final grammar must solve multiple-obviative reference rather than treating 'another obviative' as identification.
editable_elements: Every legacy verb form, exact waw morphology, participant marker, locative, plural, compound analysis, and source attribution may be replaced after research.
Strategic reanchoring, overt agreement, indexing, or limited noun repetition may be introduced when needed for participant recovery.
Exact predicate count may change, but the mounting pulse, congestion peak, reveal, short laugh, and calmer recurring coda remain protected.
The proposed assignment of Mara, Jules, and Tina to individual gags remains a design proposal until reviewed by the owner.
